note: SAMPLE mini-game library cards, hand-written for the test bench. Every card uses the same fixed format; online_module names an online module in engine/minigames.js, or null for in-person play.

cards.name: The Portrait Game
rules: The narrator describes a portrait from the hall in three short sentences.
Everyone writes down or says one detail they remember from it.
The narrator reads the description again.
Each correct detail scores a point; made-up details score nothing.
The highest scorer chooses who speaks first in the next scene.

cards.name: Alibi Charades
cards.props: Slips of paper and a hat
rules: Each player writes a silly alibi on a slip and drops it in the hat.
Take turns drawing a slip and acting it out without words.
The others have one minute to guess the alibi.
Guess it right and both the actor and the guesser score a point.
Nobody may act out their own slip.

cards.name: Twenty Questions for the Butler
rules: The host secretly picks an object hidden somewhere in the house.
Players take turns asking yes-or-no questions about it.
The host may only answer yes, no or 'the butler cannot say'.
The room has twenty questions in total to name the object.
Whoever names it wins a clue hint for their next turn.

cards.name: The Gambler's Gambit
rules: Everyone starts with 10 gold crowns. Players shoot in turn, 3 rounds each.
Come-out roll: 7 or 11 wins 3 crowns; 2, 3 or 12 loses 2.
Any other total is your point. Roll it again before a 7 to win 3 crowns.
A 7 first is a seven-out: lose 2 crowns and take a party forfeit.
The richest player wins. Crowns are only for fun, never real money.

cards.name: Twenty-One & Trouble
rules: Everyone gets two cards; the Vault Keeper shows one and hides one.
Twist to take another card, or Stick to stop. Over 21 is bust.
Twenty-one on the first two cards wins at once (the Keeper's wins the round).
The Keeper twists on 16 or less. Higher total wins; a Keeper bust means every guest standing wins.
Same total: five cards beat fewer; every other draw goes to the Keeper. No betting of any kind.

cards.name: Lexical Lanterns
rules: One team lights a hidden phrase, one letter per guest per turn.
A right letter lights every matching slot; a wrong one puts out a lantern.
Any guest may ask for one Pixie Whisper hint a phrase; it costs a lantern.
Light the whole phrase to win; if every lantern goes out, the forest keeps it.
Arcade: solve as many phrases as you can before the Sundial runs out.
